document.title: Zeitgeist Paragon Paths
document.introduction:
At level 11, you can choose one of these paths in place of a class paragon path if you meet its prerequisites. These paths grow out of the nine Zeitgeist themes, but your theme does not oblige you to choose its associated path. Each path also offers an alternative prerequisite for characters who join its tradition during play.

  For these paths’ implement powers, you can use *any weapon or implement with which you are proficient* as an implement. Their attacks and damage use your *Main Ability points* where the source refers to a primary ability score or modifier. Skill training means proficiency; History is Society and Heal is Medicine. Ability-score prerequisites of 15 become *2 points*. Use the local skill-check formula and DC table except where a rule explicitly gives a fixed DC.

  Powers below are granted at their listed levels. Other path features retain their listed timings, costs, and limitations. These imported paths include level 20 powers; the book’s warning that higher-level play is not fully verified still applies.
document.source: Zeitgeist Player’s Guide: The Investigation Begins, pp. 22–33.

paths.title: Applied Astronomist
paths.description: Skyseers can harness the distant planes’ subtle influence to change themselves, summon destructive energies, and reshape their surroundings. Hugo Theroby, the last skyseer to unlock these powers, died in 493. His unfinished Cloudwood observatory now shelters pixies with unusual magic.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.
Alternative narrative qualification requires GM confirmation; the associated theme is an independent route.

paths.prerequisiteText: Skyseer theme, or proficiency in Arcana and Nature and training by a skyseer.
paths.flavor: Skyseers can harness the distant planes’ subtle influence to change themselves, summon destructive energies, and reshape their surroundings. paths.title: Logos
paths.description: Philosophy reshapes perceptions, making the same starving child seem a burden or an investment. Some philosophers go further: recognizing the instability of belief and perception, they change reality through speech alone. The Drakran von Copenhoff supposedly learned this power from William Miller’s heretical writings and nearly seized a nation by declaring that its leaders agreed with him.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.
Alternative narrative qualification requires GM confirmation; the associated theme is an independent route.

paths.description: Ordinary guns are passé. Your modular arcano-scientific blaster stores magic, fires elemental beams and explosive projectiles, and provides an ever-growing collection of improbable tools.

paths.title: Monument of War
paths.description: Public admiration turns famous veterans into living embodiments of their wars. You can manifest remembered cannon fire or the sacrifice of a fallen comrade. Such power may be haunted by dead friends or concealed wartime shame; others seek lost glory or another chance at an escaped enemy.

paths.title: Notorious Celebrity
paths.description: If devotion strengthens gods and approval strengthens kings, fame can empower an entertainer. You attract a loyal posse, demand attention, and turn spectators’ affection into supernatural influence. Such visibility can be awkward for a constable trying to travel incognito.

paths.title: Polyhistor
paths.description: Ballistics, anatomy, motion, materials, psychology, and sociology all illuminate combat. A polyhistor combines these sciences into the right attack for each situation, pausing to observe enemies or regain composure when needed.

paths.title: Steamsuit Pilot
paths.description: Scaling a fighting contraption into wearable armor takes ingenuity and a willingness to strap yourself into a hot metal machine powered by an arcane boiler. Every pilot’s suit has its own shape and quirks, from close-fitting elven plate to a mechanized gorilla. Every machine can break.

paths.title: Urban Empath
paths.description: Cities have spirits as surely as the dead. You attune to their lingering thoughts and collective history, drawing sustenance, knowledge, and protection from streets and buildings. Your powers still work in the wilderness, but a crowded metropolis is your strongest ally.

paths.title: Vekeshi Excoriant
paths.description: A few mystics retain a sliver of Srasama’s power through devotion or the collective memory of her death. They scar and cauterize their skin with symbols of Maiden, Mother, and Crone. Some lead local cells; others follow independent callings. All recite Vekesh’s teachings nightly, renewing their purpose to protect the weak and punish abusers.

features.title: Stargazer
features.description: Gain darkvision. You cannot be blinded.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Touching the Wheel of Heaven
features.description: After an extended rest, if you spent an hour watching the night sky in the past day, roll 1d8 twice on the planar connections list, rerolling duplicates. You connect to those two planes until your next extended rest, to a maximum of 24 hours. Your connections determine the available effects of your path powers and Space Travel.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Walking the Cosmos
features.description: When you spend an action point, the next power you use this turn has unlimited range. You must still see its target or origin square.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Space Travel
features.description:
Gain both connected planes’ benefits:

- *Jiese:* Shift 1 square as a minor action.
- *Avilona:* Fly speed equal to walking speed, clumsy maneuverability.
- *Av:* Climb speed equal to walking speed, with spider climb.
- *Mavisha:* Swim speed equal to walking speed.
- *Urim:* Ignore the first square of each forced movement; you may automatically resist teleportation.
- *Apet:* Teleport 2 squares as a move action.
- *Reida:* +2 speed.
- *Nem:* Ignore difficult terrain, hovering slightly over small obstacles.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Fiat
features.description: When you spend an action point, instead of gaining an extra action, force a creature that can hear you to take an at-will standard or move action of your choice. It cannot directly damage itself, but you can place it in danger, including provoking opportunity attacks or standing under a precarious boulder.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Pathos of the Inanimate
features.description: By speech, manipulate unattended objects within 30 feet: move furniture, crack trees, open or close doors and locks, or fire guns. Move tiny things up to 30 feet as a free action, person-sized objects as a minor action, or objects filling up to a 10-foot square as a move action. Objects given a name cannot be affected; naming gives them a fragment of willpower.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Ethos of the Unwilling
features.description: Whenever you hit a creature with an attack, it takes a –2 penalty to its next attack roll.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Inventive Gunnery
features.description:
Choose a firearm type and invent a blaster of that type. It fires ordinary ammunition or unlimited force blasts. Force blasts behave like ordinary rounds but deal force damage and require no reloading.

You can have only one active blaster. If someone else fires it, it pulses; unless you regain possession within three rounds it explodes: *close burst 3; implement attack, Main Ability vs. Reflex; hit: 6[W] damage; miss: half damage*. The source does not specify the explosion’s target selection; resolve this with the GM.

If destroyed, spend 1 hour repairing it or upgrading another firearm of any type into a new blaster. You can transfer enchantments between weapons during that hour.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Autofire
features.description: When making a ranged attack with your blaster (not a close or area attack), you may fire a 10-round burst, normally using force blasts. Deal damage equal to the higher of your *Dexterity or Intelligence points* to each enemy in an *area burst 1 centered on the target*. Creatures with cover relative to you take no autofire damage.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Piercing Shot
features.description: When you spend an action point, your next blaster attack can attack each creature along a straight line from any part of your space through any part of the target’s space and up to three spaces beyond. You cannot fire the blaster again until the end of your next turn.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Rocket Launcher
features.description: Create up to five rockets per day, with a maximum of five at any time. Creating more destabilizes them all into inertness. Rockets act as grenades with *range 20/40*. Loading one into the blaster takes a standard action.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Instant Boot Camp
features.description: When you spend an action point, you and every ally who can see or hear you gain proficiency in Athletics and all simple and military weapons until the end of your next turn. Those already proficient in Athletics treat a roll of 1–7 on an Athletics check as an 8. Each affected creature can immediately stand up or drop prone, then move 2 squares.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Fearless Mein
features.description: You and allies within 5 squares gain +4 to defenses against Fear attacks and +4 to saving throws against fear effects.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Do You Want to Live Forever?
features.description: When you have no physical cover or concealment, gain cover against non-melee attacks.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Roll with a Posse
features.description:
Gain four loyal followers with the statistics on the next page. They act only at your direction. When you spend a move action, each can also spend a move action. Use an opportunity action to have one make an opportunity attack against an enemy you both see. You can spend actions to direct one member to perform a specific task, such as opening a door. Otherwise they wait, reloading their pistols if needed when given no orders.

When something damages a posse member, you may transfer that damage to yourself. If a source damages several simultaneously, protect all of them while taking the damage only once. If the same source also damages you, you can shield them without extra damage.

A member reduced below 0 HP automatically stabilizes while you live. As a minor action, spend a healing surge to restore any number of visible posse members to 1 HP. Replace a dead member the next time you are somewhere you have fans.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Center of Attention
features.description: When you spend an action point, every enemy aware of you takes –2 to attacks against targets other than you until the end of your next turn.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Crowd Effect
features.description: While watched by at least eight noncombatants, gain +5 to death saving throws. Whenever you bloody or drop an enemy, gain 5 temporary HP.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Elementary Stances
features.description: At the start of your turn, as a free action, switch to any of the five elementary stances on the next page. You can have one elementary stance and up to one stance from another source active simultaneously.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Combat Focus
features.description: Instead of a path encounter attack power, start each encounter with *three martial dice (d6s)*. Spend them on the options below or your stance options. Taking total defense as a standard action adds *three dice* if an enemy is actively fighting within 10 squares. Your pool’s maximum is *ten*; it resets to three at each encounter’s start.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Two Targets
features.description: Once on your turn when making a basic attack, spend one die to make another basic attack against a different enemy. You may stow and draw weapons between them.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Multiple Targets
features.description: When making a melee basic attack on your turn, spend two dice to target every enemy in a close burst 1. For a ranged basic attack, spend two dice to target every enemy in an area burst 1 within range. Combine with Two Targets: two dice for the melee burst, one for an extra ranged basic attack after switching weapons, and two more for that attack to affect a ranged burst.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Perfect Aim
features.description: When you spend an action point, until your turn ends you can use *Precision*: after rolling a basic attack, spend any number of martial dice, roll them, and add their sum to the attack roll.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Combat Transcendence
features.description: Your martial dice reset to *five* at the start of an encounter, and your maximum pool becomes *twelve*.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Steam & Steel
features.description:
Design a *Medium or Large suit*, no smaller than yourself. Only a creature of your size can pilot it. Entering or exiting takes a move action. A suit is inert without a pilot. Its lock opens with a key as a minor action, or a *DC 30 Thievery check* as a standard action. Lock it as a free action when entering.

Inside, your armor bonus becomes *+10*, increasing to *+11 at level 16, +12 at 21, and +14 at 26*. Apply the enhancement bonus of your worn armor or clothing under the local intrinsic-bonus rules. The suit is heavy armor, so you add neither Intelligence nor Dexterity to AC. It imposes no armor check penalty and needs no armor proficiency.

Activate or deactivate the engine as a free action on your turn. While active, its magical link lets you move, sense, and attack as if it were your body. Suit weapons reproduce your carried weapons and their enchantments.

A deactivated suit leaves you *immobilized, blinded, and helpless*. You can effectively only affect yourself or exit as a move action, except where Steam Blast explicitly gives its own disabled-suit rules.

*Medium suit:* Speed 7; lifting and carrying capacity equivalent to the source’s Strength 60, including a 600-pound light load. This does not alter checks, attacks, or damage.

*Large suit:* Speed 5; twice the Medium suit’s capacity (1,200-pound light load). Take –5 to checks needing mobility or fine control, including most Acrobatics, Athletics, and Thievery checks. Reduce each push, pull, or slide by 1 square.

*Damage:* Whenever you take damage inside, make a saving throw. After three failed saves the suit is damaged: slowed and –2 to attack, ability, and skill checks. Repair it during a short rest to restore normal operation. A pilot other than the inventor takes –5 to these saves; three failures deactivate the suit instead.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Defensive Shield (11)
features.description: When you spend an action point, gain *resist 5 all* until the start of your next turn.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Quick-Don
features.description: As a standard action, collapse the suit into a palm-sized, five-pound mechanical object. As a standard action, restore it; it may form around you and activate its engine as part of that action.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Every Building a Welcoming Home
features.description: When you spend an action point, move through man-made structures as if phasing until the end of your next turn.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Urban Bond
features.description:
In an urban environment, generally a bounded area of at least 1,000 inhabitants per square mile, you need neither food nor drink and gain +5 to Acrobatics, Athletics, and Perception checks. These benefits generally extend to within 3 miles of the urban area’s boundary.

Three times per day, spend 5 minutes communicating with buildings, roads, or other urban structures. Ask up to three questions about what they have witnessed or experienced, similarly to the _Object Reading_ ritual.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Every Window an Eye
features.description: In an urban environment, gain *tremorsense 20*. Sense the presence and location of creatures with total cover or concealment when man-made structures hide them. You can target Urban Empath powers through walls this way.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Dreadnought
features.description: Gain +2 to Will and saving throws against charm, fear, or illusion effects.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Threefold Presence
features.description: When you spend an action point, you may spend a move action this turn to move from your initial position to three locations as three versions of yourself. At the start of your next turn, choose one location to remain at; the other versions disappear. Until then, take actions and be affected as if at any of these locations. An effect hitting multiple versions affects you only once.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

features.title: Live for Vengeance
features.description: When you start a turn dying, you may spend *two healing surges* to regain HP equal to *one surge*, regaining consciousness. This counts as a failed death saving throw. Use at most *twice per encounter*.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

sections.text: *Major Affliction:* On hitting a grabbed enemy with a melee basic attack, spend two dice to make it *blinded, dazed, immobilized, or weakened* until the end of your next turn.

sections.text: *Guard:* When an enemy hits you or an adjacent ally, as an immediate interrupt spend any number of dice, roll them, and add their sum to your or that ally’s defenses against the attack. If wielding a shield, add another +2 to the sum.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

sections.text: *Evade:* When an enemy ends its movement close enough to attack you in melee, spend one die as an immediate reaction to move your speed.

limitations: Authoring and printed rules only; runtime path effects and progression are unimplemented.

sections.text: *Skirmish:* Once on your turn when making a basic attack, spend one die to move your speed. With Two Targets, you can move between attacks. Combined with Multiple Targets for a melee attack, replace its close burst with a melee basic attack against each enemy you move adjacent to during this movement.
